label: Squared Stand Collar
description: The Squared Stand collar is a band collar, worn alone: a single upright strip of cloth encircling the neck, with no leaves of any kind folding down over it. Its two front ends are cut square, meeting at the centre front across a narrow vertical gap rather than overlapping, and each end steps down where the band joins the shirt front. A single button fastens the band just below that gap. Because the band is the entire collar, its height, the crispness of its square-cut ends and the evenness of the gap between them are the whole of what there is to see, and the throat is left completely open so all of it reads clearly. The form descends from the detachable-collar shirts of Edwardian dress, where the band was made to receive a separate collar and is here finished as the collar itself.
